description: Geometric convexity of the continuous-time American put option exercise boundary in the constant-parameter Black-Scholes model; issue #175.

theorems.name: American Put Option Logarithmic Exercise Boundary Convexity
theorems.description: For positive strike K, risk-free interest rate r and volatility sigma, and constant dividend yield 0 <= q <= r, the logarithm log(B(tau)/K) of the continuous-time American put option exercise boundary is convex in positive time-to-expiry tau. B is defined from the optimal-stopping value on the completed usual filtration of the constructed Brownian motion. The conclusion is geometric convexity, not strict logarithmic curvature or existence of classical second derivatives. The literature recorded convexity as open for 0 < q < r (proved at q = 0, disproved for q > r); this entry covers that whole region, resolving the open problem.

code.lean:
import MathFin.BlackScholes.AmericanPut.Stopping.PhysicalBoundaryConvexity

open Set
open MathFin.BlackScholes.AmericanPut.Stopping

theorem american_put_log_boundary_convex {K r q σ : ℝ}
    (hK : 0 < K) (hr : 0 < r) (hq : 0 ≤ q) (hqr : q ≤ r) (hσ : 0 < σ) :
    ConvexOn ℝ (Ioi 0)
      (fun τ : ℝ => Real.log (brownianUsualExerciseBoundary K r q σ τ.toNNReal / K)) :=
  MathFin.BlackScholes.AmericanPut.Stopping.brownianUsualLogBoundary_convexOn hK hr hq hqr hσ

metadata.reference: Robert Martin, Log-convexity of the exercise boundary of an American put option; source development https://github.com/robertmartin8/AmericanPutConvexity/tree/9b2b208520341a63b64eef43c1ecb3c5708a8e63; MathFin issue #175.
metadata.formalization_scope: Derived from the concrete stopping-value definition, not from an assumed classical free-boundary solution or a convexity specification. Admissible rules are all stopping times of the constructed completed usual Brownian filtration with values pointwise bounded by the horizon; AEHorizonValue proves equality with the value and threshold obtained from extended stopping times bounded by the horizon only almost surely. The value uses GBM with drift r-q and discount rate r. The proof derives the normalized boundary and its line-interval property using a straight-line comparison, a parabolic three-point argument and a terminal barrier, then proves geometric convexity and rescales to physical units. Covers q=0 and q=r as well as 0<q<r, only at positive time-to-expiry. Does not assert universality over arbitrary probability-space representations, C2 regularity, strict log-convexity, or a result for q>r.

theorems.name: American Put Option Exercise Boundary Strict Convexity
theorems.description: For positive strike K, risk-free interest rate r and volatility sigma, and constant dividend yield 0 <= q <= r, the continuous-time American put option exercise boundary B(tau) is strictly convex in positive time-to-expiry tau. B is defined from the optimal-stopping value on the completed usual filtration of the constructed Brownian motion. Strict convexity is in the chord-inequality sense; the statement does not assert a classical second derivative or B'' > 0. The literature recorded convexity as open for 0 < q < r (proved at q = 0, disproved for q > r); this entry covers that whole region, resolving the open problem.

metadata.formalization_scope: Derived for the same actual stopping boundary as the logarithmic-convexity entry. The proof first obtains nonstrict convexity of the logarithmic boundary using only its nonincrease. A terminal barrier excludes a flat tail, so convexity and nonincrease imply strict decrease; strict convexity of the exponential then yields strict convexity of the stock-price boundary. The physical-unit theorem assumes only K>0, r>0, sigma>0 and 0<=q<=r. Its domain is positive time-to-expiry. No boundary-smoothness premise is imposed, and no classical second-derivative or q>r conclusion is claimed.

theorems.name: American Put Verification: A Contact Rule Attains the Initial Value Iff the Stopped Candidate Is a Martingale
theorems.description: Let U be a bounded continuous supermartingale on a filtered finite measure space and theta an admissible stopping rule at whose time U equals the American put's discounted reward almost surely. Then the expected reward at theta equals the integral of U at time 0 if and only if the process U stopped at theta, t maps to U(min(t, theta)), is a martingale. The statement does not assume that U dominates the reward, and it does not identify U with the put's value.

code.lean:
import MathFin.BlackScholes.AmericanPut.Stopping.OptimalStoppedMartingale

open MeasureTheory
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin.BlackScholes.AmericanPut.Stopping

theorem expected_reward_eq_initial_iff_stopped_martingale {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
    {𝓕 : Filtration ℝ≥0 ‹MeasurableSpace Ω›} {P : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure P]
    {W U : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} {K r q σ S C : ℝ} {T : ℝ≥0}
    (hU : Supermartingale U 𝓕 P) (hc : ∀ ω, Continuous (fun t => U t ω))
    (hb : ∀ t ω, ‖U t ω‖ ≤ C) (θ : StoppingRule 𝓕 T)
    (hcontact : ∀ᵐ ω ∂P, U (θ.time ω) ω = putReward W K r q σ S θ.time ω) :
    (∫ ω, putReward W K r q σ S θ.time ω ∂P) = ∫ ω, U 0 ω ∂P ↔
      Martingale (fun t ω => U (min t (θ.time ω)) ω) 𝓕 P :=
  expectedReward_eq_initial_iff_stopped_martingale hU hc hb θ hcontact

metadata.reference: Verification theorem for optimal stopping (Peskir and Shiryaev, Optimal Stopping and Free-Boundary Problems, Ch. I): the stopped value process of an optimal rule is a martingale; MathFin values-review backlog item 1.
metadata.formalization_scope: The reward process W and the parameters K, r, q, sigma, S are arbitrary: only the contact identity U(theta) = putReward at theta is used. The forward direction is the ordered optional-sampling argument (every earlier bounded rule has the same mean, then pasting two observation times on a past event gives the set-integral criterion for a martingale); the reverse direction is bounded continuous-path optional stopping for a martingale. Boundedness and path continuity of U are required by both directions; dominating the reward by U is not.
